idiom_name: data class snapshots + List<Version>.binarySearchBy on the effective date (java.time keys)
implementation_notes: Versions are Kotlin data classes - val properties plus the generated copy() give the working copy the update path needs - and the continuity holds the list sorted by an effective java.time key. The as-of lookup is kotlin.collections.binarySearchBy, which returns either the exact index or the inverted insertion point, so the temporal collection is the sorted list and the predecessor lookup is stdlib arithmetic; prefer it to firstOrNull { } scans once the history exceeds a handful of versions. Keys stay JVM date types (LocalDate/Instant); kotlinx-datetime is the alternative only when the model must stay independent of the JVM.
pitfalls: data class copy() is shallow: a List or MutableList member is shared with the previous version, so mutating it rewrites history - keep members immutable or copy the collections explicitly.
binarySearchBy returns the inverted insertion point (-index - 1); computing the predecessor as -i - 2 is the classic off-by-one, and -i - 1 == 0 must yield null rather than index -1.

binarySearchBy assumes the list is sorted by the very key being searched: appending without sorting makes lookups return wrong versions silently, because an unsorted result is undefined rather than an error.
LocalDate keys are timezone-free while database timestamps are usually UTC instants - pick one representation and convert at the boundary, or effective dates shift by the server offset.
